ADR-001: Postgres as the ledger store

The journal needs a store that can refuse to lie. We choose Postgres and lean on its strongest isolation level rather than building correctness in application code.

Context

The ledger needs serializable transactions and strong constraints: a posting touches several account rows plus the outbox, and two concurrent postings against the same account must never interleave into an unbalanced state. Whatever we pick also has to be operable by a two-person team.

Options considered

OptionForAgainst
Postgres True SERIALIZABLE isolation, deferrable constraints, boring ops, team fluency Single-writer ceiling near 10k TPS per partition
DynamoDB Managed scale, predictable latency 25-item transaction cap forces app-side balancing; weaker constraint model
Event store (custom) Journal is naturally an event log We would own consistency, snapshots, and tooling — highest risk for least leverage

Decision

Decision

Use Postgres with SERIALIZABLE isolation for journal writes. Conflicting postings fail with a serialization error and are retried by the ledger core; the database — not our code — proves that no unbalanced interleaving exists.

Consequences

  • Simple operational story: one database technology across the platform.
  • Retry loops are mandatory in the ledger core — serialization failures are normal, not exceptional.
  • Constraints (balanced legs, currency checks) live in the schema and cannot be bypassed by new code paths.
Revisit when

Sustained journal write load approaches 10k TPS on a single partition — the trigger to design account-range sharding (tracked in the ledger roadmap).
